name: rdap
desc: Command-line client for the Registration Data Access Protocol
why: A client for RDAP, the modern successor to WHOIS, a protocol door most people never open.

brief.what_it_is: OpenRDAP is a command line client for the Registration Data Access Protocol (RDAP), written in Go. You give it a domain, IP address, AS number, entity tag, or a few other query types, and it looks up the registration record over HTTP. Output can be text, raw JSON, or WHOIS-style text for domain queries. It finds the right RDAP server automatically from IANA bootstrap data, and you can name a server yourself with -s.
brief.why_it_exists: RDAP is presented as a replacement for WHOIS, returning domain and IP registration data in JSON over HTTP instead of the older plain-text WHOIS protocol. The homepage calls it a command line client for that protocol and says the same site also hosts the Go library and a public RDAP service at rdap.net.
brief.how_it_works: The client detects the query type from the input (domain, ip, asn), finds the authoritative RDAP server through bootstrap data from data.iana.org or a custom URL, and sends the query over HTTP. It can cache the bootstrap files on disk. Results come back as RDAP JSON, which it renders as text, raw JSON, or WHOIS style.

brief.install_notes: Requires Go 1.20 or later; the README points to golang.org for the compiler. Installation is via go install, not Homebrew. The bootstrap cache is optional and stored under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/openrdap, falling back to ~/.cache/openrdap. X.509 client authentication is supported, but the README gives no setup steps for it. Advanced query types need a server URL passed with -s, since not all servers support every type.
brief.standout: Automatic server discovery through IANA bootstrap data means a plain rdap example.com works without knowing which registry runs the zone. It also covers the full set of RDAP query types, including searches, from one small binary with WHOIS-style output for people who want the old format.
brief.status: unknown. The README and homepage show no release version, date, or last-commit information. The GitHub README still links a Travis CI badge at travis-ci.org, which suggests the CI setup may be old, but that is not evidence of current activity.
brief.caveats: Needs a Go toolchain to install; no prebuilt binary or Homebrew note appears in what I read. Search queries such as abc*.com are not yet bootstrapped, so they need -s. The homepage lists support for the future ICANN layered access specification as planned, not done. Some servers do not support all query types. Search wildcards are only partly covered by automatic detection.
